original_question: A pure O-sequence is the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal, where all maximal monomials have the same degree; its type is the number of maximal monomials. What is the largest type t for which every pure O-sequence is unimodal, without imposing any restriction on codimension or socle degree? In particular, does unimodality always hold for pure O-sequences of type 2?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Open Problem 1: determine the largest type t for which all pure O-sequences are unimodal, independently of codimension or socle degree; in particular, whether pure O-sequences of type 2 are unimodal in any codimension. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly targets the global unimodality problem with no restriction on codimension or socle degree, and it also preserves the paper's highlighted special case asking whether type 2 always forces unimodality. The wording is essentially a faithful paraphrase of Open Problem 1. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone in the paper's sense, the object should be introduced as a finite, nonempty monomial order ideal X of monic monomials in variables y_1,...,y_r, closed under divisibility, with h(X)=(h_0=1,h_1,...,h_e) counting monomials by degree. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
The common degree e of the maximal monomials should be named explicitly as the socle degree. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The codimension r should be identified explicitly as the number of variables (equivalently, after removing linear forms in the algebraic model). ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
Unimodal should be spelled out using the paper's convention: nondecreasing up to some degree and nonincreasing thereafter. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

If the equivalent algebraic language is used, one should specify that pure O-sequences are exactly the Hilbert functions of standard graded artinian monomial level algebras R/I, with type equal to dim_K Soc(R/I). ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The paper notes that whether a sequence is a pure O-sequence does not depend on the field K, so no field restriction is part of this open problem, even though Section 2 later passes to an infinite field for the inverse-system setup. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a finite pure monomial order ideal in variables y_1,...,y_r, and write its h-vector as h(X)=(1,h_1,...,h_e), where e is the common degree of the maximal monomials of X (the socle degree) and the type t is the number of maximal monomials. A sequence is unimodal if it is nondecreasing up to some index and nonincreasing thereafter. What is the largest integer t such that every pure O-sequence of type t is unimodal, independently of the codimension r and the socle degree e? In particular, is every pure O-sequence of type 2 unimodal in arbitrary codimension? ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the inverse-system correspondence of Section 2, if A=K[x_1,...,x_r]/I is a standard graded artinian monomial level algebra with socle concentrated in degree e and dim_K Soc(A)=t, what is the largest type t for which the Hilbert function h_A=(1,h_1,...,h_e) is always unimodal, independently of r and e? In particular, must every type-2 artinian monomial level algebra have a unimodal Hilbert function? ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
justification: The nearest official target is Open Problem 1 in Section 5, not a broader neighboring problem. Section 2 supplies the hidden definitions and the motivation for the type-2 clause: Theorem 2.3 gives unimodality for type 1; Theorem 2.12(a) proves the type-2 case in codimension 3; Theorem 2.14(b) proves the type-2 case in codimension 4; and immediately after Theorem 2.14 the paper explicitly asks whether all pure O-sequences of type 2 and arbitrary codimension are unimodal. This is exactly the path your draft is following, so only definitional sharpening was needed. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
